bill.title: Proposing a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution of the United States.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Restrictions on federal borrowing and debt issuance would directly affect the market for Treasury securities, a core product for banks and asset managers.
Balanced-budget requirements could constrain discretionary spending including defense appropriations, though military conflicts receive an explicit waiver.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment requiring the federal government to balance its budget each year unless three-fifths of both the House and Senate vote to allow deficit spending. It would also require a three-fifths supermajority to raise the debt ceiling and mandate that the President submit a balanced budget annually. These requirements could be waived during declared wars or serious military threats to national security.

bill.title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025

industries.rationale: The bill directly increases advance cost-sharing payments and expands eligibility for agricultural producers recovering from natural disasters.
Expanded federal disaster assistance may affect demand for private agricultural and forestry insurance products.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands two federal programs that help farmers and forest landowners recover from natural disasters. It increases the percentage of costs that can be paid in advance—from 25% to as much as 75%—before repair work begins, and broadens the types of damage that qualify for assistance, including wildfire damage even when the fire was not naturally caused. Recipients would have 180 days to use advance payments.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 466.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research grants and regulatory pathways for development of drugs and therapies targeting ALS and neurodegenerative diseases.
Providers treating ALS patients may see changes in available investigational therapies and clinical trial access, though the bill focuses primarily on research and regulatory processes.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data on experimental drugs and mandates that the Food and Drug Administration publish a five-year plan describing how it will help develop and approve therapies for these rare diseases. The bill also continues a public-private partnership between federal agencies and outside organizations working on neurodegenerative disease treatments.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone who uses the internet.
